html:
Paekche, also spelled Baekje, was a Korean kingdom in the southwest of the peninsula from 18 BCE to 660 CE, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.

Tradition says Onjo, a son of the founder of Goguryeo, founded it near today's Seoul. Its fortunes followed its wars with its neighbours:

  • 300s: at its height it held most of western Korea.
  • 475: Goguryeo took its capital, and the court moved south to Ungjin, now Gongju.
  • 538: it moved again, to Sabi, now Buyeo.

Paekche was a sea power with close ties to southern China and to Japan. Its scholars, monks and craftsmen carried writing, Buddhism and building skills to the Yamato court, and Buddhism reached Japan officially as a gift from a Paekche king in the 500s.

In 660 a Tang and Silla alliance took Sabi. A Japanese fleet sent to restore the kingdom was destroyed at the Battle of Baekgang in 663, and many Paekche nobles fled to Japan.
sum: Paekche, also spelled Baekje, was a Korean kingdom in the southwest of the peninsula from 18 BCE to 660 CE, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
